standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter together with the classical description: Pic(X) is an extension of Z by the divisible group Pic^0(X) of dimension g, whose n-torsion is (Z/n)^{2g}

core_obligations: Collect the identifications (proof lines 11165-11209): the author runs the Kummer sequence, uses the known cohomology of the multiplicative group and of the structure sheaf on a smooth projective curve, and reads off the four groups in the first display.

Noncanonical identifications (proof lines 11212-11217): since mu_n is isomorphic to the constant sheaf Z/n, the author shows that the kernel of multiplication by n on Pic^0(X) is (Z/n)^{2g}, which gives the second display.
proof_roadmap: Run the Kummer sequence and plug in the known cohomology of G_m and of the structure sheaf on a smooth projective curve.
Read off the groups in degrees zero to two and the vanishing above.
Use the structure of Pic^0(X) to compute its n-torsion and obtain the noncanonical identifications.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the etale cohomology of the roots of unity on a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field: mu_n in degree zero, the n-torsion of Pic^0(X) in degree one, Z/n in degree two and zero beyond, together with the noncanonical identifications obtained from mu_n = Z/n (statement lines 11134-11163). The proof runs the Kummer sequence against the known cohomology of the multiplicative group and of the structure sheaf (proof lines 11165-11209) and then computes the n-torsion of Pic^0(X) to obtain the numerical version (proof lines 11212-11217). The non-formal content is the combination of the Kummer sequence with the structure of the Picard group. The claim is H2: a computation from cited theorems, carried out in full.
